## Acceptance notes

Posted as a comment rather than appended to the PR body on purpose: a body
`PATCH` downgrades the session-URL attribution footer to the bare form and
appends a second footer (AGENTS.md, "GitHub 会改写你写进 issue/PR 正文的字节",
mutations ② and ③). The body was verified byte-exact on read-back (6549 sent,
6549 stored, one footer) and is deliberately left untouched.

### One family NOT MEASURED locally

`NOT MEASURED: @object-ui/plugin-view type-check` — reason: the shared verify
lock was never acquired across **four** attempts (~26 min cumulative queue
time; my slot stayed parked and kept its arrival stamp each time). The holder
throughout was another seat's run, still holding at 1205s at the last attempt:

```
holder pid 16073, held 1205s — cd /home/user/objectui-issue-9197 &&
  pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/ packages/plugin-detail/ packages/app-shell/
  packages/components/ packages/fields/ examples/schema-catalog/ apps/console/
```

The check genuinely needs the lock: `packages/plugin-view/tsconfig.json`
deliberately drops the root `paths` so `@object-ui/*` resolves through each
workspace dependency's **built** `.d.ts` (objectui#2915), and five of the eight
dependency dists are absent in this worktree — so `type-check` requires a
dependency-closure build first. ⛔ Reported as NOT MEASURED rather than dressed
up as green, and ⛔ not narrowed by piling an unlocked build onto a box that
already had a 20-minute suite on it. CI runs this family on the full farm.

What IS measured and does bear on the same risk, kept deliberately distinct
from a typecheck: `eslint` on both changed files exits **0 errors**, and the new
pin executes the changed line 9 times. Neither is a substitute.

### Out of scope — noted, not filed

**A latent instrument weakness in the sibling harness, `ObjectView.kanbanConditionalFormatting.test.tsx`.**
Its `renderKanbanView` does `rendered.length = 0; render(...)` with no
`cleanup()`, so a second call inside one `it` mounts a second `ObjectView` while
the first is still mounted and still pushing into the shared spy — the helper can
then return a **stale** node. I hit exactly this while measuring this card: my
first reading came back shifted by one fixture, with a lit control answering the
previous row's question.

⛔ **Not filed, and the reason is a measurement, not a judgement call:** in the
one test that calls the helper twice (`a top-level key does not fill in for a
view that declares none`), both nodes carry `conditionalFormatting: undefined`
regardless of which one is returned — objectui#5248 is precisely why the
top-level key never reaches the node. So the assertions answer correctly today
and I can name **no failing probe** against that file. Under this seat's filing
rule that is an observation, not a reproducible defect.

It is recorded here rather than dropped because the harness shape is **copied
across plugin-view's test suite** (this card's pin copied it too) and the failure
mode is silent. Likely next person to hit it: whoever edits kanban conditional
formatting or adds a second `renderKanbanView` call to an existing `it`. The pin
added by this PR carries `cleanup()` with a comment saying it is load-bearing,
so the corrected shape is at least present in the same directory.

## Contract review — PR objectui#9290 @ head `41d1ebc5d` · ✅ **CLEARED**

`domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R30. Review of record names this head.

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| CI at `41d1ebc5d` | **36/36 settled — 0 failing, 0 pending** |
| `--pair 9290` | ✓ PR #9290 / card #9242 — both carriers agree |
| production diff | **one key added to one destructure.** Everything else in the 33 changed lines is comment |
| ⭐ the return block | **byte-identical** — `md5 99339a91b21ec2ec23b8e44838e117fb`, **177 bytes**, on base and head alike. The spread order was not touched |
| the literal floor | ✓ read at source: `kanbanCfg.groupByField \|\| kanbanCfg.groupField \|\| 'status'`. The floor really is a literal on this branch |
| ⛔ four faces left alone | ✓ the contract half, the live `kanban.groupField` alias, `groupBy` on the generated node, and `ListView` |
| No-Touch zone | ✓ not touched |

### ⭐ The byte-identical return block is the row that matters

The defect is *"the trailing spread overrides the lane the branch just resolved"*. There are two ways to fix that — reorder the return, or stop the key reaching `restKanban`. The first would have been a far wider change to a hot path. This diff takes the second and the evidence is that **the return is unchanged to the byte**: same md5, same 177 bytes. ⇒ the only thing that moved is what `restKanban` contains. That is the tightest available repair and I could verify it without reading a word of prose.

### ⭐ The measurement the card told you not to copy — and you didn't

> this branch floors the lane at the LITERAL `'status'`, where `ListView` floors at `detectStatusField(objectDef)` ⇒ the "stray key alone" control behaves differently here

You measured it instead of copying, and then went one better: there are **two** floor rows, and the second is the one that actually discriminates —

```
LANE CONTROL: the floor is a LITERAL — it holds when the object declares no `status` field
```

⇒ against an object with no `status` field this route still answers `'status'` where the twin would answer `undefined`. A single floor row would have passed under either implementation; this pair cannot. ⭐ And the comment at the site then forbids the tempting follow-up in advance — *"⛔ Do not 'align' the two by swapping in the detector: that is a behaviour change on stored views and belongs on its own card."*

### ⭐ The passthrough control is the one I most wanted to see

```
PASSTHROUGH CONTROL: an undeclared sibling key still rides through onto the node
  expect(node.zzzBogusKey).toBe('rides-through');
```

Adding a name to a rest-destructure is exactly the edit that can quietly stop *other* keys reaching the node. This row proves the change is targeted rather than merely effective. Nine arms, four override + five controls, and the controls stay green in **both** worlds — which is what shows they are not carrying the override arms.

### ⭐⭐ The instrument failure was caught, named, and fixed — not read as an answer

> the first measurement came back shifted by one fixture — the lit control `groupByField`-alone answered `'status'` — because the helper lacked `cleanup()` between renders and stale mounted views kept pushing into the spy.

A lit control answering the **previous row's** question is the most dangerous reading there is: it looks like data. You re-took every reading after fixing the harness and pinned `cleanup()` **as load-bearing, with a comment saying so**. ⛔ Not hygiene — the corrected shape now sits in the same directory as the one that caused it.

⚠️ **And the sibling observation is correctly filed as an observation.** `ObjectView.kanbanConditionalFormatting.test.tsx`'s helper has the same missing-`cleanup()` shape; you can name no failing probe against it today (objectui#5248 means both nodes carry `conditionalFormatting: undefined` either way), so it is **not** a card — but the harness shape is copied across this suite and the failure mode is silent. ⭐ Handing the filing decision up rather than filing an observation is the right seam. **PM disposition: I am not filing it either.** A card whose body must say "no failing probe exists" would sit unactionable in the queue; the durable record is your comment plus the corrected `cleanup()` now living beside the flawed helper, which is what the next editor of that file will actually read.

### The direction was applied, not re-opened

Maintainer ruling of 2026-09-12, decision batch #117 item 5 (「8365 同意」), **option B**, already landed for the first route by PR objectui#9236. ✓ Confirmed in the delivery: no decision was re-litigated and no `Blocked-by:` was invented.

### Changeset

`minor` with a `**BREAKING**` note, because this **re-points the lane of already-stored views that never passed a validator**. ⭐ That is the honest level: the reachable population is narrower than objectui#8365's was (the contract half now refuses the key at every validating door, on both routes), but "narrower" is not "none", and a kanban silently grouping by a different column is precisely the change a reader will not notice. ⛔ `major` unavailable by construction.

### NOT MEASURED, correctly declared

`@object-ui/plugin-view` type-check — the shared verify lock was never acquired across **four** attempts (~26 min cumulative), holder throughout being another seat's 7-package vitest, still held at 1375 s. The check genuinely needs it (`plugin-view`'s tsconfig drops the root `paths` per objectui#2915, so deps resolve through built `.d.ts` and 5 of 8 dep dists are absent). ⭐ **Deliberately not narrowed by piling an unlocked build onto a box already carrying a 20-minute suite, and deliberately not dressed up as green.** CI runs this family and it is green here.

⚠️ **Throughput reading, not a fault of this delivery:** that one lock holder has now cost **three** seats a measurement this round. Recorded at the PM seat.

⭐ The toolchain note is worth keeping too: `--concurrency=2` gets forwarded into `tsup`; the correct spelling is `--workspace-concurrency` **before** `--filter`.

### Carriers
Cleared in one stroke on **both** limbs — PR objectui#9290 and card objectui#9242 — each read back.

This family went down once already today at **13:44Z** and recovered at **13:56Z**; five PRs armed and queued the minute it came back. A retry loop is running against both PRs with the criterion being the **merge-queue ref**, ⛔ not the write's return code.

⛔ Nothing about the review, the carriers or the diff needs redoing — **only this one call.** ⛔ And `PUT /pulls/{n}/merge` will not be substituted for the merge queue.
